domain_handling: poor (splits fiscal years, percentages, currency)
advantages_observed: Treebank rules handle contractions and punctuation faithfully; mature and fast
limitations_observed: no domain awareness: splits 7.4%, FY2025-26 components and currency symbols
suitable_downstream_use: baseline experiments, teaching comparison, generic indexing

domain_handling: partial (keeps numbers, splits hyphens and fiscal ranges)
advantages_observed: trained orthographic rules; fastest; keeps 6.50 and repo-rate whole
limitations_observed: still splits percentages, fiscal-year ranges and hyphenated compounds
suitable_downstream_use: fast indexing when domain expressions are handled as extra fields

domain_handling: strong (purpose-built rules, inspectable)
advantages_observed: 17 ordered, inspectable rules; preserves fiscal years, percentages, currency, scale words
limitations_observed: no linguistic model: cannot disambiguate, and rules are tuned to this domain
suitable_downstream_use: exact indexing of fiscal years, percentages and currency amounts

domain_handling: strong (domain layer over a standard tokenizer)
advantages_observed: keeps NLTK's linguistic behaviour while protecting domain expressions
limitations_observed: three-pass cost (protect/tokenize/repair) and private-use sentinels in between
suitable_downstream_use: Phase 3 inverted index over domain-aware terms

domain_handling: neutral, but can delete modality/domain nouns (see stopword analysis)
limitations_observed: deletes protected financial terms (see domain_stopword_analysis.csv)
suitable_downstream_use: query-side filtering only, never on protected financial terms

domain_handling: reduces inflections; can over-stem financial terms

domain_handling: reduces inflections; slightly more aggressive than Porter

domain_handling: very aggressive; highest collision rate
